summary: The chronological-dispatch gate landed asserting rule text that was never committed, so master was red on every clean checkout while the author's working tree was green

action: Ship the contract text the gate asserts (the three contract documents now declare the dependency-ordered rule)
Count and report each non-conforming contract document independently instead of through a shared counter

evidence.note: the fix that made a clean checkout green again

title: Prove a gate against the committed tree, never the working tree: reconstruct the files it asserts on from the merge commit and run it there

remediation: add a gate-proof step that reconstructs the asserted files from the merge commit and runs the check there, so a dirty tree can never manufacture a pass
title: Every new gate ships a clean-checkout proof

summary: Issue #148 was reported complete with passing test evidence while every file it claimed to deliver was still untracked; nothing had shipped

action: Ship the work the completion report claimed: the leaderboard session registry and its suite
Confirm every claimed file with `git ls-files --error-unmatch <file>` before reporting an issue done

evidence.note: the delivery the misreported claim had not shipped

title: Work that is not committed does not exist: a passing run in the working tree is not evidence of delivery

summary: Two lanes worked one issue in parallel and shipped a byte-identical 53-line change to the three contract documents; one merge was pure waste

action: Record and validate a single claim before work starts, so an in-flight issue is locked and a second claim fails loudly

evidence.note: PR #159 landed the claim gate for issue #157

title: A rule that exists only in prose is advisory: concurrent lanes need a claim lock, not a declaration gate

remediation: publish the lane claim to the steering channel when it is taken, so two lanes on one issue see the overlap before a pull request is opened
title: Make lane overlap visible at claim time, not at merge time

summary: The claim audit retroactively failed a completed issue ("#139: claimed after it was closed") because the replay compared a historical claim event against the present board snapshot

action: Treat a released claim as finished history: the closed-issue and milestone-frontier rules apply only to a claim still live at audit time

evidence.note: PR #172 fixed the replay in governance/dispatch/claims.py

title: A frontier is a point-in-time property: never recompute a historical decision from today's snapshot

summary: The claim gate reported closed issue #139 as the eligible frontier from a board snapshot that was 19 minutes old; the reader consumed stale data as truth because it had no freshness rule

action: Add a snapshot-staleness check to the claim gate and store claims conflict-free, so an answer derived from a stale snapshot is refused rather than returned

remediation: state the age a point-in-time artifact may reach before it is refused, and read the timestamp the artifact already carries (issue #170)
title: A snapshot's timestamp is part of its meaning
